answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (PoroTomo DAS, Brady Hot Springs, March 2016; read-only report via report.py):

- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), spanning 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z — 3.314% of the time window.
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc).
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days.
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016).

CALIBRATED probabilities (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — the LBNL catalogue calibration):
  b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198, P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 5.236e-06, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719
  b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922,  P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 0.0002155, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809
  b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474,   P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 0.0006484, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated DAS magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated LBNL-catalogue estimates give P(Mw>=5.5) of roughly 1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 per year depending on the b scenario (b = 1.0 to 0.65), i.e. a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 earthquake is very unlikely under the calibrated model. The DAS-based figure of 0.07842/yr is an upper bound only: DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and all 62 detections are treated as events at/above Mc, so it systematically over-counts and should not be read as a calibrated probability.
